# Fixed-five compression certificate calculations

This calculation document holds the long rational input tables for Theorems E.8.1ah, E.8.1ak and E.8.1al in [the thermodynamics and area-law section](../../../appendices/appendix_e_thermo_area_law.md). Their complete projection models, operational scopes, hypotheses, exact optima, attaining channels, algebraic identities and verification arguments remain in the paper. This document supplies the density, box and sparse-dual inputs, with the same indexing and rational values. Short parameter, algebraic-root, row-definition and identity tables remain in the respective theorems.

Every rational is exact. Closed boxes include their shared faces. Sparse pairs $(j:m)$ give the printed integer numerator at index $j$, and all omitted entries vanish. A dyadic word specifies a path by the precise subdivision rule stated in its section. No numerical search or optimization output substitutes for the finite witnesses.

<a id="rank-four-density-witnesses"></a>

## Rank-four rational density boxes

**Rational corner certificate.** The boxes and densities below supply the finite part of the preceding proof. For each row, $l,h\in\mathbb Q^4$ are the lower and upper endpoints and $\omega=(w,p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4)$ is a probability vector. Each row has $0\le l_i\le h_i\le1$, $\sum\omega_i=1$ and $0\le\omega_i\le2/5$. The largest printed weight is $129213419/400000000$.

Set $K=10^{30}$ and define
$$
\underline r(x)=K^{-1}\left\lfloor\sqrt{\left\lfloor K^2x\right\rfloor}\right\rfloor\quad(x\ge0),
\qquad \overline g(x)=1-\underline r(1-x)\quad(0\le x<1).
$$
Then $\underline r(x)\le\sqrt x$ and $1-\sqrt{1-x}\le\overline g(x)$. For one printed row put
$$
\begin{gathered}
u=\max_i p_i,\quad M=\max_i\omega_i,\quad D_0=1-M\sum_i h_i>0,\quad
\beta=\frac1{4D_0\underline r(D_0)},\\
m_i=(l_i+h_i)/2,\qquad c=\frac{\sum_i m_ip_i}{\sum_i m_i},\qquad
Q_j=\sum_{i=5-j}^4(1-l_i),\quad Q_0=0.
\end{gathered}
$$
At each of the sixteen corners $a_i\in\{l_i,h_i\}$ let $r_i=1-a_i$, $z=\sum_i a_ip_i$ and $V=\sum_i a_i(p_i-c)^2$. The five bounds are
$$
\begin{aligned}
B_j&=\overline g(z)+\overline g\!\left(wr_1+u\sum_{i=5-j}^4r_i\right)
 +\sum_{i=2}^{4-j}\overline g(wr_i)+\beta VQ_j &&(0\le j<4),\\
B_4&=\overline g(z)+\overline g\!\left(u\sum_{i=1}^4r_i\right)+\beta VQ_4.
\end{aligned}
$$
Empty sums are zero. Substitution gives $B_j\le232461961848107/500000000000000$ in all $2885\cdot16\cdot5=230800$ cases. The convex-corner and branch argument in the proof extends these bounds to each whole box. All 2,885 witnesses are as follows.

## Rank-four analytic boxes

Each row is a closed box $[l,h]\subset\mathbb Q^4$, in the same coordinate order as the density table. These are the remaining forty-five nonempty leaves of the same closed cover. Every box lies in $[92/125,369/500]^4$, where Theorem E.8.1ah supplies the analytic inequality. The theorem retains its complete midpoint subdivision, emptiness test and all scalar margins.

<a id="eleven-to-five-closed-cover"></a>

## Eleven-to-five complete dyadic cover

The table is the closed-cover input of Theorem E.8.1ak, with coordinates $r,d$, $u=r+d$ and $v=r$. A row index in a sparse multiplier tuple is the zero-based spectral-row index in that theorem's displayed constraint matrix; the corresponding exact coefficient is the printed integer divided by $5\cdot2^{44}$. The first twelve primal coordinates lie in $[0,1]$, the next five in $[0,u+v]$, and coordinate seventeen is the objective variable $t$. The following copied conventions make every box, chamber and sparse multiplier unambiguous; their proofs remain in the theorem.

For an exterior corner with integer multipliers $m_j$, put $D=5\cdot2^{44}$, $R=\sum_jm_jA_j(u,v)$ and $b=\sum_jm_jb_j$. Each printed vector has $R_{17}=-D$; its five norm multipliers sum to $-D$ and lie in $[-2D/5,0]$. The first twelve coordinates of $x$ belong to $[0,1]$, and the next five to $[0,u+v]$. Consequently moving every residual to its adverse endpoint gives the valid bound
$$
L(u,v)=u+v+1+\frac{b+\sum_{j=0}^{11}\min(-R_j,0)+(u+v)\sum_{j=12}^{16}\min(-R_j,0)}D.
$$
The coefficient of $t$ is exact, so no bound on $t$ is used. For $[r_l,r_u]\times[d_l,d_u]$ substitute $(u,v)=(r_l+d_l,r_l)$ and multiply by $Z_l=1+1/r_u+1/(r_u+d_u)$. Every corner row below has $Z_lL\ge32487/5000$.

A dyadic box word is a sequence of coordinate/side pairs. Pairs $00,01$ select the lower, upper midpoint half in $r$; $10,11$ do so in $d$. Start at $[1,11/2]\times[0,43/2]$. Types $P,S,T,C$ mean path chamber, symmetric chamber, trace, corner. A $T$ row gives the exact bound $Z_l[(r_l+d_l)/5+r_l+1]$. A $C$ row gives its sparse integer multipliers. For a $P$ row, the whole-box chamber tests are
$$
d_l\ge r_u(r_u-1),\quad d_u\le r_l^2,\quad
2r_l(r_u+d_u)+2(r_u+d_u)+2r_l^2+2r_l-3(r_u+d_u)^2\ge0.
$$
An $S$ row lies wholly in $[6/5,3/2]\times[0,1/50]$. The analytic chamber proofs above therefore apply on those entire boxes.

<a id="sixteen-to-five-proof-tree"></a>

## Sixteen-to-five rational proof tree

The table is the complete rational proof tree of Theorem E.8.1al. The four coordinates are the ordered normalized coefficient coordinates used in that theorem; all inequality indices refer to its explicit inequality-row table, and the four equality entries retain their displayed order. A missing sparse multiplier is zero. Every entry is an exact integer numerator. The root, tightening order, terminal types, multiplier denominator and target are as follows; the corresponding residual identities and whole-box proof remain in the theorem.

**Complete rational proof tree.** The table below lists nodes in preorder, lower child first. Start from $[69/1000,793/1000]^4$. Before reading a node, perform five rounds of the following order/normalization tightening, in the printed update order:
$$
\begin{gathered}
l_i\leftarrow\max(l_i,l_{i-1})\ (i=1,2,3),\quad
h_i\leftarrow\min(h_i,h_{i+1})\ (i=2,1,0),\\
h_i\leftarrow\min\left(h_i,\frac{1-\sum_{j<i}l_j}{4-i}\right),\quad
l_i\leftarrow\max\left(l_i,\frac{1-\sum_{j>i}h_j}{i+1}\right),\\
l_i\leftarrow\max\left(l_i,1-\sum_{j\ne i}h_j\right),\quad
h_i\leftarrow\min\left(h_i,1-\sum_{j\ne i}l_j\right)\quad(i=0,1,2,3).
\end{gathered}
$$
An inverted interval is empty. A row $S_j$ splits the tightened box at its midpoint in coordinate $j$, with both closed children. Types $E,T,T_N,O,A,H,C,C_N,C_H$ denote empty, trace, normalized trace, original chamber, adjacent chamber, hybrid chamber, corner dual, normalized corner dual and height-improved corner dual. For $H$, the additional symbol $O,A,U$ means the original conjunction, adjacent conjunction or proved switching union. Its polynomial and centered-gradient tests are those of part IV.

For a corner row, $(i:m)$ means inequality multiplier $m/10^{12}$; the last column gives all four equality numerators with the same denominator. The residual compensation and optional normalization/height bonuses are the exact formulas in part IV. The five norm numerators sum to $-10^{12}$ and lie in $[-2\cdot10^{12}/5,0]$, and the residual on $t$ is exactly $-10^{12}$. Every indicated lower bound is at least $12553554/10^6$.

<a id="additional-spectral-and-scalar-calculations"></a>

# Spectral row and scalar calculation tables

These additional expansions belong to Theorems E.8.1ak–al in [the thermodynamics and area-law section](../../../appendices/appendix_e_thermo_area_law.md). The exact row formulas, recursive membership rule, scalar polynomial definitions, negative-remainder recurrence, sign arguments, algebraic identities and attaining-channel proof remain in the paper. The sections below retain the selected row ordering and the longer computed coefficient and interval data.

<a id="eleven-to-five-spectral-rows"></a>

## Eleven-to-five selected spectral rows

The rows are the selected finite spectral constraints used by Theorem E.8.1ak. Row $j$ is exactly the zero-based row used by every multiplier numerator in the closed-cover calculation. This is a selected Horn list, not a claim that it lists every necessary Horn inequality. The recursive Horn test and row semantics remain in the theorem; they are repeated here to define all names and coefficients unambiguously.

**Analytic duals and finite exterior certificate.** A sparse list $(j:m)$ assigns multiplier $m/(5\cdot2^{44})$ to row $j$ of the table below; absent coefficients are zero. Equality multipliers have unrestricted sign; every inequality multiplier is nonpositive. Row indices start at zero.

Use the eighteen spectral coordinates
$$
x=(a_{01},\ldots,a_{04},a_{11},\ldots,a_{14},a_{21},\ldots,a_{24},g_1,\ldots,g_5,t).
$$
For a spectral triple $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$, the row indexed by $(I,J,K)$ is $\sum_{k\in K}\gamma_k-\sum_{i\in I}\alpha_i-\sum_{j\in J}\beta_j\le0$; the trace row is equality with every index. Projection rows use $(a_0,a_1,(1-a_{24},\ldots,1-a_{21}))$ in dimension four; output rows use $(u a_0\oplus0,v a_1\oplus0,g)$ in dimension five. Names $a_i1\le1$, $a_i4\ge0$, $\mathrm{order}_{ij}$ and $g_j\mathrm{order}$ denote respectively $a_{i1}\le1$, $-a_{i4}\le0$, $a_{i,j+2}-a_{i,j+1}\le0$ and $g_{j+2}-g_{j+1}\le0$, with zero-based name indices. Norm row $t_j$ is
$$
t-g_{j+1}-w(a_2\oplus0)_{5-j}\le0\qquad(0\le j<5).
$$
These definitions specify each affine row $A_j(u,v)x\le b_j$ exactly.

The Horn triples used here have a finite recursive definition. For $1\le r<n$, take increasing $r$-subsets $I,J,K\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}$ satisfying $\sum I+\sum J-\sum K=r(r+1)/2$. Retain such a triple exactly when, for every $1\le q<r$ and every retained dimension-$r$ triple $(A,B,C)$ of size $q$,
$$
\sum_{a\in A}i_a+\sum_{b\in B}j_b\le\sum_{c\in C}k_c+q(q+1)/2.
$$
For $r=1$ the additional tests are empty. Every Horn triple in the row table belongs to this recursively defined set.

<a id="sixteen-to-five-subresultant-expansion"></a>

## Sixteen-to-five degree-one subresultant expansion

This is the complete coefficient expansion of the degree-one subresultant $S_1(x,y)$ for the derivative polynomials of Theorem E.8.1al. The theorem retains the exact definitions of $p_{\rm sc},q_{\rm sc},A,B$ and the generating identity $S_1=32x^4[A(x)y+B(x)]$, as well as $y=-B/A$ and the full resultant identity. Thus the display below is an expansion of already defined polynomials, with the variable and coefficient order unchanged.

$$

<a id="sixteen-to-five-stationary-sturm-coefficients"></a>

## Sixteen-to-five stationary Sturm coefficients

For a coefficient tuple $(c_0,\ldots,c_d)$, its polynomial is $c_0x^d+c_1x^{d-1}+\cdots+c_d$, including every displayed zero coefficient. The member index starts at zero. The starting polynomial and negative-remainder recurrence remain in Theorem E.8.1al; the tuples below give its exact positively rescaled primitive members. The boundary chain, endpoint variations and root-isolating intervals remain beside that proof.

Thus $S_1=32x^4(Ay+B)$, and the recovered ordinate is $y=-B/A$. The primitive coefficient lists below are in descending powers, including zero coefficients. Their positive rescalings form the Sturm chains defined by $S_0=P$, $S_1=P'$ and $S_{j+1}=-\operatorname{rem}(S_{j-1},S_j)$. The boundary chain starts with $75x^4+136x^3-192x^2-64x+75$. This recurrence and the exact coefficients fix every endpoint sign.
